t: Section 40152(c) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 13941) is amended by striking “$5,000,000” and all that follows and inserting “$5,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2018.”.

fable.w: This section only amends an authorization of appropriations by changing the dollar amount and the fiscal years it covers. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision. There is no real tempting reading here; the Violence Against Women Act reference does not itself create any outside-party process.
fable.s: is amended by striking “$5,000,000” and all that follows and inserting “$5,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2018.”

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment to an appropriations statute, changing the authorized funding amount for specific fiscal years. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text contains no reference to participation by non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: Section 40152(c) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 13941) is amended by striking “$5,000,000” and all that follows and inserting “$5,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2018.”.

opus.w: This section is only a technical amendment that renews the appropriations authorization at $5,000,000 per year for fiscal years 2014 through 2018. It does not require or allow any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government. The underlying program's subject matter is not enough to make this funding provision participation.
opus.s: is amended by striking “$5,000,000” and all that follows and inserting “$5,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2018.”.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking:** The tempting reading is that the cited statute, Violence Against Women Act § 40152 (42 U.S.C. 13941, which covers education and training programs), involves outside groups like courts or nonprofits, so this section might be participation. That reading fails because this section only changes the amount and fiscal years of an appropriations authorization. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. No one outside the federal government is brought into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a statute that funds programs for victims of violence implicitly involves public participation, or that the mention of "Violence Against Women Act" suggests public hearings. However, the text itself is purely a fiscal amendment changing a dollar amount and a time range. It contains no procedural requirements for consultation, comment periods, hearings, or advisory boards.
